context: SYSTEM-ENGINEERING defines a tool-independent Project Operating System (CORE, SCHEMAS, COMMANDS, AGENTS). OpenCode is the initial execution environment. The INTEGRATIONS/opencode adapter is currently documented but not implemented. Surfaces adopted in MASTER-SYSTEM-DESIGN-01 and MASTER-SYSTEM-ROADMAP-ARCHITECT-01: se.py = adapter/orchestrator; OpenCode = consumer runtime; generated OpenCode assets must never be the source of truth.
problem: How does OpenCode consume the Master System without coupling CORE/SCHEMAS to a specific tool, and without OpenCode needing to read arbitrary folders?

pros: Single source of truth remains the contracts
Commands and agents are thin wrappers over se.py
Generated assets live in standard OpenCode locations (.opencode/, ~/.config/opencode/)
cons: Requires implementing and maintaining the adapter
Generated assets must be regenerated on contract changes

options_considered.option: Inline re-implementation of contracts inside OpenCode config
cons: Two sources of truth that drift

options_considered.option: Make OpenCode read contracts directly from arbitrary paths
cons: OpenCode does not load agents/commands/skills from arbitrary paths
Breaks restriction: no dependence on OpenCode reading arbitrary folders

decision: Use an adapter-only bridge. INTEGRATIONS/opencode defines two responsibilities: (1) generation of OpenCode assets (.opencode/agent|command|skill, opencode.json, AGENTS.md) from the contracts, and (2) execution where OpenCode commands/agents invoke the reference CLI (se.py). CORE and SCHEMAS remain free of tool-specific concepts.
reason: It satisfies the closed architectural decisions: se.py = adapter/orchestrator, OpenCode = consumer runtime, generated assets derived from contracts, and no reliance on OpenCode reading arbitrary folders. It is the only option that keeps a single source of truth and preserves tool independence.
consequences: The OpenCode adapter must be implemented in SCRIPTS/se_core as commands (se adapter opencode) and reused by se init. Generated artifacts must be versioned and drift-checked by se validate. Permission enforcement maps the Master System permission model onto OpenCode tool permissions.
